name: Napa Valley

contains: Oak Knoll District of Napa Valley

climate: Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

keyfacts: Napa Valley was established as the nation's second AVA in 1981 and covers all of Napa County except the portion northeast of Putah Creek and Lake Berryessa.
Grape varieties grown include Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Merlot and Zinfandel.
As of 2024, there are seventeen sub-AVAs within Napa Valley, and the Oakville and Rutherford AVAs lie on the Rutherford Bench.
The open southern end of the valley floor is cooler because of San Pablo Bay, while the sheltered northern end is often much warmer.
Soils in the south are mainly sediments from San Pablo Bay, while the north has a large volume of volcanic lava and ash.
The climate is Mediterranean, with hot dry summers and cool wet winters, and daily summer fog that usually lingers until mid-morning.

blurb.text: California's first AVA and the nation's second, in a Mediterranean climate. Cabernet Sauvignon is the main grape in Napa County, followed by Chardonnay and Merlot. Napa gained wide recognition at the Paris Wine Tasting of 1976.
